issue.title: gateway/gui: cannot configure passHeaders or replyHeaders for plugin-backed providers in Web UI
issue.body:
### Problem Description

When integrating custom gateways, reverse proxies, or relay providers via community/custom plugins (plugin providers), there is currently no way to configure `passHeaders` or `replyHeaders` through the Web UI.

Inspecting the codebase reveals:
1. **Core Gateway Support**: Magpie's core gateway (`internal/provider/requestheaders.go` and `internal/provider/account.go`) already fully supports reading `passHeaders` and `replyHeaders` from `providers.json` and passing client headers directly upstream.
2. **Web UI Missing Input**: In `internal/gui/assets/app.js` (`#9311`), plugin-backed accounts (`p.account`) use a dedicated render branch that omits the "Advanced" section's `passHeaders` ("Request headers to pass") and `replyHeaders` ("Reply headers") inputs. Those fields are currently only available in the custom provider (`else` branch, `#9564`) form.
3. **No Declarative Plugin API**: The plugin specification (`auth.loader` or `plugin.Provider`) does not expose a `passHeaders` field, so a plugin cannot declare default headers to forward out of the box either.

Because client headers like `x-claude-code-session-id` or `x-client-request-id` are stripped by Magpie's default whitelist unless explicitly listed in `passHeaders`, users are forced to manually edit `/data/magpie/providers.json` inside the container to make plugin gateways work with CLI agents.

---

### Suggested Fix / Enhancement

Either of the following (or both) would resolve the issue cleanly:

1. **Expose `passHeaders` / `replyHeaders` in the Web UI for plugin accounts**:
   Include the "Request headers to pass" and "Reply headers" inputs in the plugin account editor modal (under Advanced), aligned with custom providers.
2. **Support declarative `passHeaders` in plugin definitions**:
   Allow plugins to declare default passable headers in `config` or `auth.loader` (e.g. `headers` / `passHeaders`), which Magpie can merge into the provider configuration automatically upon installation.

comments.body:
A fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5359-plugin-account-header-fields), commit [aca455708](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/aca455708d5a651590cc7be8620fa95e9e2742a6), based on `ed0ab567`.

The gap was the editor, not the gateway: the account branch of the provider editor returned before the custom-provider Advanced fields were built, so a plugin-backed provider never showed "Reply headers"/"Request headers to pass" and its saves sent neither key, even though `accountSettings`, the save handler and the gateway already carried them.

The two fields now come from shared helpers used by both branches with the same order, labels, hints and error focus. Plugin-served accounts (moved built-ins included) show them; saves always send both arrays, so emptying a box clears it, while ordinary account saves still send neither key and keep their old values. `Authorization`/`Set-Cookie` are still refused and never forwarded.

New tests through the real plugin host, offline, with a fake vendor: a configured pass header reaches the vendor while an unlisted one and `Authorization` do not; a configured reply header reaches the agent while an unlisted one and `Set-Cookie` do not. A GUI test covers save, clear, refusal and that secrets are not handed back. Both packages pass `-race`, along with the adjacent plugin-page/provider-save tests; offline `nogui` vet and build pass. Not covered: Playwright DOM tests for the two header inputs (the module is not resolvable here) — the editor rendering is covered by code review and the API-level tests. AI-assisted implementation and review.
